extracted.intended_audience: Covered entities and recipients of Federal financial assistance in health programs (healthcare providers, health insurers/QHP issuers, Exchanges, brokers/agents, compliance and legal staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural rules implementing Section 1557 of the ACA governing nondiscrimination in health programs and activities, including coverage/benefit design, marketing, use of decision support tools, telehealth, notification procedures for religious/conscience objections, and enforcement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory coverage/exclusions related to gender transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must not have or implement a categorical coverage exclusion or limitation for all health services related to gender transition or other gender-affirming care; must not otherwise deny or limit coverage, deny or limit coverage of a claim, or impose additional cost sharing or other limitations or restrictions on coverage for specific health services related to gender transition or other gender-affirming care if such denial, limitation, or restriction results in discrimination on the basis of sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text enumerates that exclusions/limitations for gender-affirming care that result in sex‑based discrimination are prohibited. The general prohibition in paragraph (a) is not limited by the enumerated forms in paragraph (b). Legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons (see separate criterion) may justify denial if not a pretext for discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on benefit designs leading to segregation/institutionalization of people with disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must not have or implement benefit designs that do not provide or administer health insurance coverage or other health-related coverage in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of qualified individuals with disabilities, including practices that result in the serious risk of institutionalization or segregation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefit design must aim for most integrated setting appropriate to individual needs; designs that create serious risk of institutionalization or segregation are discriminatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons for coverage decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this section requires coverage of any health service where the covered entity has a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason for denying or limiting coverage or determining that such health service fails to meet applicable coverage requirements, including reasonable medical management techniques such as medical necessity requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such coverage denial or limitation must not be based on unlawful animus or bias, or constitute a pretext for discrimination. Nothing here precludes relying on protections described in §§ 92.3 and 92.302.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sex discrimination related to marital/parental/family status (§92.208)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether an individual satisfies any policy or criterion regarding access to its health programs or activities, a covered entity must not take an individual's sex into account in applying any rule concerning an individual's current, perceived, potential, or past marital, parental, or family status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to rules regarding access to health programs/activities; sex (as defined at §92.101(a)(2)) cannot be used in applying marital/parental/family status rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination on the basis of association (§92.209)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must not exclude from participation in, deny the benefits of, or otherwise discriminate against an individual or entity in its health programs and activities on the basis of the respective race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability of the individual and another person with whom the individual or entity has a relationship or association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects individuals from discrimination based on relationship or association with persons of protected characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in patient care decision support tools (§92.210)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability in its health programs or activities through the use of patient care decision support tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires ongoing duty to make reasonable efforts to: (1) identify uses of decision support tools that employ input variables or factors that measure race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability; and (2) mitigate the risk of discrimination resulting from use of each identified tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in telehealth services (§92.211)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered entity must not, in delivery of its health programs and activities through telehealth services, discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telehealth delivery must comply with nondiscrimination obligations just as in-person services do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement mechanisms (applicability of other civil-rights statutes) (§92.301)
rubrics_metrics.description: The enforcement mechanisms available for and provided under title VI, title IX, section 504, and the Age Discrimination Act shall apply for purposes of section 1557 as implemented by this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates which existing enforcement procedures and remedies are available to enforce Section 1557 obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification procedure for asserted religious freedom or conscience exemptions (§92.302) — content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient seeking assurance that Federal religious freedom and conscience protections excuse application of particular provision(s) of this part must submit a written notification to the Director of OCR that includes: (1) the particular provision(s) from which the recipient asserts exemption; (2) the legal basis supporting the exemption, including governing standards under applicable Federal religious freedom/conscience protections (e.g., RFRA, ACA provisions, Church/Coats‑Snowe/Weldon Amendments); and (3) the factual basis supporting the exemption including identification of the conflict between the recipient's beliefs and the requirements, and specific contexts, procedures, or services that purportedly violate those beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification may be provided at any time (before or during an investigation). The legal basis should reference governing standards; the factual basis should identify contexts or specific services at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification procedure for religious freedom or conscience exemptions (§92.302) — temporary exemption and process
rubrics_metrics.description: A temporary exemption from administrative investigation and enforcement takes effect upon submission of the notification. If received before an investigation, OCR must email-confirm receipt within 30 days and then work expeditiously to reach a determination. If received during an investigation, the temporary exemption will exempt conduct as applied to the specific contexts identified during pendency of OCR's review and will serve as a defense until final determination or conclusion of the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary exemption is limited to particular provision(s) as applied to the specific contexts identified in the notification. The notification does not preclude OCR's subsequent determination; procedures for appeal and finality (45 CFR part 81) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR determination, appeal, and finality for exemption requests (§92.302)
rubrics_metrics.description: If OCR determines to provide assurance of exemption or modified application, OCR will provide the determination in writing; if granted, recipient will be considered exempt from OCR administrative investigation/enforcement as applied to specified contexts. An adverse determination may be appealed under administrative procedures at 45 CFR part 81; the temporary exemption expires upon a final decision under 45 CFR part 81. A determination is not final for purposes of judicial review until after a final decision under 45 CFR part 81.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes administrative appeal path and effect on temporary exemption and judicial review timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for recipients and State Exchanges (§92.303)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural provisions applicable to title VI apply with respect to administrative enforcement actions against health programs and activities of recipients and State Exchanges concerning discrimination under section 1557 or this part. If OCR receives a complaint over which it lacks jurisdiction, it shall promptly notify the complainant and make reasonable efforts to refer the complaint to the appropriate Federal entity. When a recipient or State Exchange fails to provide requested information in a timely, complete, and accurate manner, OCR may, after attempting voluntary resolution, find noncompliance and initiate enforcement procedures including fund suspension or termination and other actions authorized by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes cooperation in investigations, referral obligations, and that failure to provide information can trigger enforcement steps found at 45 CFR 80.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for health programs/activities administered by the Department (§92.304) — access to records
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 504 procedures apply with respect to administrative enforcement actions against the Department. The Department must permit OCR access to books, records, accounts, other sources of information, and facilities as may be pertinent to ascertain compliance with section 1557 or this part. Where required information is in exclusive possession of another agency/institution/person that refuses to furnish it, the Department must certify and set forth efforts made to obtain it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asserted considerations of privacy or confidentiality may not operate to bar OCR from evaluating or seeking to enforce compliance. Information of a confidential nature obtained in connection with compliance evaluation or enforcement shall not be disclosed except where necessary under the law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on intimidation, retaliation, and confidentiality protections (§92.304)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department must not intimidate, threaten, coerce, retaliate, or otherwise discriminate against any individual or entity for the purpose of interfering with any right or privilege secured by section 1557 or this part, or because such person made a complaint, testified, assisted, or participated in any manner in an investigation, proceeding or hearing. The identity of complainants must be kept confidential by OCR in accordance with applicable Federal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms non-retaliation obligations and OCR confidentiality protections for complainants; violation may give rise to enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing and benefit design prohibition for health insurance issuers (Part 147 §147.104(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A health insurance issuer and its officials, employees, agents and representatives must comply with any applicable State marketing laws and cannot employ marketing practices or benefit designs that will have the effect of discouraging the enrollment of individuals with significant health needs in health insurance coverage or discriminate based on an individual's race, color, national origin, present or predicted disability, age, sex (including sex characteristics, intersex traits; pregnancy or related conditions; sexual orientation; gender identity; and sex stereotypes), expected length of life, degree of medical dependency, quality of life, or other health conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad prohibition covering both marketing practices and benefit designs that effectively discourage enrollment or produce discrimination against persons with significant health needs or other protected/status characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑interference and non‑discrimination standards for Exchanges (§155.120)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges and related entities must not interfere with Federal law and must not discriminate based on race, color, national origin, disability, age, or sex (with sex defined to include sex characteristics, intersex traits; pregnancy or related conditions; sexual orientation; gender identity; and sex stereotypes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that Exchanges must follow nondiscrimination obligations and not adopt policies or practices that discriminate on protected grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents, brokers, and web-brokers conduct standard (§155.220(j)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents, brokers, and web-brokers assisting enrollment must provide consumers with correct information, without omission of material fact, regarding Federally-facilitated Exchanges, QHPs, and insurance affordability programs, and refrain from marketing or conduct that is misleading (including direct enrollment websites that could mislead consumers into believing they are visiting HealthCare.gov), coercive, or discriminates based on race, color, national origin, disability, age, or sex (with sex defined inclusively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places affirmative informational and non-misleading obligations on intermediaries; explicitly prohibits coercive or discriminatory marketing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: QHP issuer non-discrimination requirement (§156.200(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A QHP issuer must not, with respect to its QHP, discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, disability, age, or sex (which includes discrimination on the basis of sex characteristics, including intersex traits; pregnancy or related conditions; sexual orientation; gender identity; and sex stereotypes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly applies nondiscrimination requirements to QHP issuers and the coverage they offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct enrollment information and conduct requirement for QHP issuers (§156.1230(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a QHP issuer facilitates direct enrollment in a manner considered to be through the Exchange, the issuer must provide consumers with correct information, without omission of material fact, regarding the Federally-facilitated Exchanges, QHPs offered through the Exchanges, and insurance affordability programs, and refrain from marketing or conduct that is misleading (including websites HHS determines could mislead consumers into believing they are visiting HealthCare.gov), coercive, or discriminates based on protected characteristics including sex (with inclusive definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors agent/broker obligations for QHP issuers when performing direct enrollment; HHS may determine particular websites or practices to be misleading.
